# The Elven Highroad — records, repairs and a road worth sharing

Original fantasy episodes. The supplied 84 Scripture cards and 72 older adventures remain unchanged. These scenes distinguish remembered Scripture, moral reflection and ordinary physical actions. Exploration and return travel remain open.

## whiteledge-sereth · Sereth · A record taller than its keeper

Sereth must bend to hear you. Her pale traveling coat has been mended at the cuffs; a mountain flower is caught in its hem. Behind her, the record-house rises from the terrace like a folded wing.

“Carverbough has been accused of closing the beacon roads. Our clean copy says so. Aurel says our clean copy is wrong.” She turns the copper clasp in her fingers. “I signed it. I should like very much to find that I was careful.”

#### Success

“The earlier ledger is in the back archive, beyond the galleries. The crossing’s date and the seal’s date cannot both be right.”

The courier bell above her has lost its clapper; a smaller hand-bell hangs beside it. “Read the ledger. Bring me the dates. Then we can lower the record tube at the outside bell.”

[if flag:highroad-charter]“Take the corrected copy north to Lethir in Carverbough. Tell him whose seal was on the wrong one.”[/if]

#### Short

“Climb the record-house steps. Compare the two dates on the record in the back archive, then return to the bell outside for the corrected copy.”

## whiteledge-aerin · Aerin · The sky and the small letters

Aerin has spread a chart on the reading terrace. The mountains drawn along its edge are much smaller than the mountains beyond her shoulder. “A good chart knows what it has left out.” She points to a narrow blank in the old road. “A courier could still pass there. A procession could not.”

#### Success

“There are people who mistake a long memory for a complete memory. I am one of them on Tuesdays.” She lends you a dry place to read. “The sky speaks of its Maker. It does not authorize my next guess about a neighbor.”

#### Short

“The old road is narrow, not gone. The sky declares its Maker; it does not certify my guesses about my neighbors.”

## whiteledge-aurel · Aurel · A bear with mud on his paws

The bear steps aside before you need to ask. A little mountain mud stains the white fur above his enormous paws. “Aurel,” he says, with a careful bow. “Keeper of a ford. Today, merely a traveler whose lunch has escaped its wrapping.”

He has carried a broken road plate all the way uphill. Its underside bears a maker’s date that the clean record does not mention.

#### Success

“The ford was chest-deep when the timber cart reached us. Three Carvers brought it through, singing to keep their footing. I remember the song; I remember that date.” He turns the plate over. There is a new gouge beside the old stamp.

He recovers his lunch and offers half. “Mereth has the matching ledger in the record-house. Take the dates to Sereth. And if Bracken offers you a shorter road, agree on the price before the first hill. He charged me again at the second.”

#### Short

“The old maker’s date is under the bridge plate. Mereth keeps its matching ledger in the record-house. Bring both dates to Sereth.”

## whiteledge-librarian · Mereth · The page without a name

Mereth is rubbing wax from a once-covered margin. “We copied the accusation beautifully. We did not copy the witness’s name.” She lays the rubbing beside the lamp. Under the smooth seal, another set of letters survives.

#### Success

“The dated road record waits in the back archive, on the eastern side. Aurel’s bridge plate is older than the closure order. Here — the same maker’s stamp, under both seals.” She holds the page toward the lamp. The missing name has left a groove through three sheets.

Footsteps stop beyond the outer door. Mereth folds the rubbing into your hand. “Read the archive page, then take the outside bell to Sereth. Have her lower a corrected copy. Carverbough will need it before their beacon can answer.”

#### Short

“Read the dated record in the eastern back archive. Then use the outside bell: Sereth can send a corrected copy to Carverbough.”

## whiteledge-record · The two dates beneath the seal

The upper page accuses the Carvers of breaking the northern crossing. Beneath its seal, the old maker’s date is still legible: the crossing was already closed before the Carvers’ convoy arrived. A witness’s name has been scraped away.

You lay the rubbing beside the page. The crossing closed three days before the Carver convoy arrived. Someone has scraped out the witness’s name and sealed the accusation over it. A fleck of blue thread clings to the wax.

#### Success

You copy the two dates, including the uncertainty. Sereth has asked for a correction rather than a new boast. Outside by the record-house, the old road bell still holds the tube for authenticated copies.

## whiteledge-bell · The bell and the unearned signature

Sereth sets her seal beside your dated copy. “I wanted the accusation to be somebody else’s fault. Read with me, then help me put this correction where a courier can carry it.” The record tube is caught behind the bell’s slack counterweight. Its release is visible from the little stair landing.

#### Success

The remembered words give the conversation room for honesty. Sereth names her mistake without asking you to make it smaller. You steady the counterweight, turn its plain iron catch and lower the tube. She signs the correction; you keep a copy with both dates. Carry it north to the Carver Elves. No one has repaired a bridge merely by saying the right words.

#### Hint

Read a discovered passage that connects with the choice here. Its words invite reflection; the physical repair still needs careful hands.

#### Failure

The catch slips before the weight is seated. You step back to the landing with a bruised hand. One heart is lost; every card, dated record and recovered part stays with you. Read, rest or try again.

## carver-lethir · Lethir · The house that holds other houses

Lethir braces a split lantern-cradle against the oak. Two empty sockets shine where the brass pin should be. Beyond the houses a messenger bell rings once, then stops.

“Greenwood has missed the evening signal three nights running. We shall not send another courier into that dark.”

#### Success

“Find our brass pin beside the bottom stair of the south carving-house. Bring it to me here, or to the beacon workbench east of the main road, near the spring.”

He turns the damaged cradle. Someone has cut through its locking shoulder with a narrow saw. “Mira is in the north guildhouse, up the winding stairs. Ask her about the cut. And bring Whiteledge’s corrected road record; it tells us how much weight this frame must carry.”

[if flag:highroad-pin-delivered]“The pin is set aside at the workbench. We still have the cradle to raise.”[/if]
[if flag:carver-beacon-repaired]The bell sounds again. This time Lethir lets it finish.[/if]

#### Short

“Find the brass pin at the south carving-house’s bottom stair. Give it to me, or bring it to the beacon workbench east of the main road. We also need Whiteledge’s corrected record.”

## carver-mira · Mira · The hand that asks for help

Mira has laid three lengths of broken timber on her bench. The middle one bears a clean saw-cut; the others splintered when the lantern fell. Two fingers of her left hand are bound in a narrow splint.

“Storm damage runs with the grain,” she says. “This cut goes across it.”

#### Success

She fits the pieces together. A leaf-shaped guild stamp has been scored through on the underside.

“Pip dropped the brass pin beside the south carving-house’s bottom stair. Find it and give it to Lethir, the master outside this guildhouse. He can also receive it at the beacon workbench, east of the main road near the spring. Bring Sereth’s corrected record from Whiteledge.”

From the rear gallery comes a low work-song:

“Through root and rafter — runs the grain;
hold fast the light through leaf and rain.”

Mira follows your glance. “Back-right stairs for the upper rooms. Save me the window seat if you get there first.”

#### Short

“Find the brass pin beside the south carving-house’s bottom stair. Give it to Lethir outside the north guildhouse, or at the eastern beacon workbench. Bring Whiteledge’s corrected record too.”

## carver-nael · Nael · What a badge cannot promise

Nael rolls a timber sled away from the eastern stair. Under its canvas lie six lamp-posts, each stamped with a village name. One name has been planed away.

“A Whiteledge convoy brought these yesterday. Their captain had a fine seal and no answer about that missing name.”

#### Success

She prises a blue thread from a nail-hole and folds it into her glove. “The same cloth was caught under our northern gate. If the watch-ring in Greenwood is still listening, its keeper may know the convoy.”

“Lethir handles the beacon. I keep this eastern road open. Tell me if the stair gives you trouble; I would rather move a sled than mend a traveler.”

#### Short

“Lethir is the beacon keeper, outside the north guildhouse. I guard the eastern road. After the repair, take the north road to Greenwood’s watch-ring; ask about a convoy carrying blue cloth.”

## carver-pip · Pip · The impressively lost pin

Pip is flat on his stomach beneath a root, fishing with a hooked twig. He withdraws a beetle, apologizes to it, and tries again.

“The brass pin went that way. I was demonstrating a catch. It was an excellent catch until the catching part.”

#### Success

He points to the south carving-house, below its winding stair. “Beside the bottom step. There is a little acorn mark on the head.”

He has already wrapped the beacon glass in his best scarf. “Lethir takes the pin. I take this. If I drop them both, Nael says she will make me carry the tree.”

#### Short

“The pin is beside the bottom stair of the south carving-house. Give it to Lethir, the beacon keeper at the north guildhouse, or take it to his eastern workbench.”

## carver-counterweight · A joint made to carry a neighbor

The beacon cradle hangs from a rope above Lethir’s workbench. Pip crouches behind the lamp glass; Mira watches the cut in the locking shoulder. The line begins to creak.

“Pin ready,” says Lethir. “Record open. Take the weight when I count three.”

#### Success

On three, you lift. The cradle slews toward the spring; Mira catches its edge with the crook of her good arm. Lethir drives the pin home.

For a breath nothing happens. Then a pale line runs through the glass and leaps north between the trees. Pip forgets to breathe until a distant bell answers.

Beneath the damaged shoulder, Mira finds a freight mark: a war camel beneath a seven-pointed brand. You take a rubbing. “Greenwood first,” says Lethir. “Let its keeper see what rode this road.”

#### Hint

The pin must be delivered and Whiteledge’s corrected record brought here. Choose a discovered passage, recall it, then help Lethir raise and secure the cradle.

#### Failure

The shoulder slips. Mira shouts; you let the cradle fall back onto its trestle. One heart is lost. The delivered pin and road record remain ready for another attempt.

## carver-commission · A light toward Greenwood

The highroad rises toward Greenwood. The repaired beacon behind you carries an honest message at last; the watch-ring ahead has not answered. A warning about Man Ghouls has been pinned beneath the route mark.

#### Success

Take the north road. The woodland watch-ring is the next part of the journey. The Ashland giants and their war-camel roads lie farther beyond; this correction is a beginning, not the whole repair.

## carver-loft-book · The book at the moon window

Someone has left a blank page between accounts of two failed repairs. In the margin: “Leave room for the person who learns after you.” Beneath the moon window, the village sounds arrive softened by leaves.

#### Success

You may rest with the words here, explore the sleeping alcoves, or return by the lower-right stair. A house can make room for a guest without making the guest prove useful first.
